payload.title: Waist-to-height ratio
payload.summary:
The waist-to-height ratio (WHtR, or WSR: waist-to-stature ratio) is the waist circumference divided by body height, both measured in the same units.
WHtR is a measure of the distribution of body fat. Higher values of WHtR indicate higher risk of obesity-related cardiovascular diseases, which are correlated with both total fat mass (adiposity)  and abdominal obesity.


== History ==
In 1996, WHtR was first suggested by Ashwell and Cole as a simple health risk assessment tool because "it was identified as a proxy for harmful central adiposity since WHtR was correlated with abdominal CT scan". A boundary value of 0.5 was proposed to indicate increased risk.
